title: Bharata and the fawn
word: reading the Isha in the original
hook: a king leaves everything to remember God, then rescues a fawn
carry: what the mind keeps remembering, it holds at the end

segments.voice: Yesterday, preya and shreya: the lovely can hide the good, and Nachiketa turning down Death's gold. Now the Isha's last two verses, and a king who forgot what to remember.
screen: `PREYA AND SHREYA.` · `NOW: THE LAST TWO VERSES.`

segments.voice: King Bharata, the Bhagavata says, ruled so well that the land itself was named after him. Then he gave it all up and went to live by a river in the forest, to spend his days remembering the Lord. One morning a pregnant deer, startled by a lion's roar, leaps the river. Her fawn slips from her into the water, and she dies soon after. Bharata scoops up the fawn. He feeds it, worries over it, searches for it when it wanders. Slowly his prayers get shorter, and his thoughts of the fawn get longer. When he dies, the fawn is at his side, and it's the fawn he's thinking of.
screen: `A KING LEAVES EVERYTHING.` → `A FAWN IN THE RIVER.` → `HIS LAST THOUGHT: THE FAWN.`

segments.voice: So, the story says, he's born next as a deer, one that remembers who he was and stays near the sages. Hindus tell it with a warning and a tenderness: what the mind keeps returning to, it carries to the end. The Bhagavad Gita says whatever one remembers on leaving the body, to that one goes, having always dwelt on it. Always: the end follows the whole life. Now Isha seventeen. Vayur anilam amritam: breath, to the deathless wind. And this body, ending in ash. Then: krato smara, kritam smara. Mind, remember. Remember what was done. Verse eighteen turns to the fire: agne naya supatha. Agni, lead us by the good path. Many readers, Shankara among them, hear these lines as a prayer at the moment of death. It's why Hindus give the body to Agni in cremation, and why many families say God's name beside someone who is dying: so the name the mind has practiced all its life is there at the end. Smarana, remembering, is a daily practice for exactly this. And the week, once more: Shankara in the alley. Gargi's nots. Shvetaketu, proud. Janaka with a crown. Markandeya in the flood. Nachiketa refusing gold. One Upanishad, read slowly to its last request.
screen: `WHAT THE MIND RETURNS TO, IT CARRIES.` · `BODY TO ASH. KRATO SMARA: MIND, REMEMBER.` · `AGNE NAYA SUPATHA: LEAD US.` · `A WEEK OF THE ISHA, IN SIX STORIES.`

segments.voice: Count back through today on your fingers: one thing you did this morning, one at midday, one just now. Let each come back plainly, without judging it: smara, remember what was done. If you pray, end with the name your family says, Ram, Krishna, Shiva, Om, softly, three times. If not, end with one thing you'd want to remember. Then rest the hands.
Reading the Isha in the original, to its last line: krato smara, mind, remember, and agne naya supatha, Agni, lead us by the good path.

howItsDone: Agne naya supatha is also a Rig Vedic verse to Agni, and some Hindus recite it at the fire; at a deathbed many families chant God's name or play it softly, and the body is given to Agni in cremation.

fork.reveal: the Gita says what one has always dwelt on, one goes to; the Isha's dying prayer says mind, remember. the chanting keeps the lifelong name close.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: smara, remember, from Isha 17's krato smara; smarana, remembering God, is a daily practice.

trapdoor: what you thought: an ancient text ends with the big answer.

what a scholar hears: krato and agne are vocatives; verse eighteen is also Rig Veda 1.189.1; Gita 8.6's sada tad-bhava-bhavitah makes the end follow lifelong habit, which Bharata's story (Bhagavata 5.8) dramatizes.

chat.meaning: Bharata left a kingdom to remember the Lord, but his last thoughts were of a fawn. The Gita and Isha 17 teach that what the mind practices remembering is what it holds at the end; Nani's daily name is that practice.

tie.story: King Bharata left his kingdom to remember the Lord, grew so attached to a fawn that it filled his last thoughts, and was born next as a deer.
